clue.text: Saturday never comes without supporters

definitions.meaning: if Saturday never arrives, the day before it goes on for ever: FRI(day) endless
having nobody on your side, alone and unbacked

explanation.surface: A lament that the weekend's big match is played to empty stands.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic reading: when Saturday never comes, Friday (FRI) is ENDLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no supporters has no allies or companions at all, which is the sense of having no pals.

clue.text: Fine, loose material

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
lax means loose or slack

explanation.surface: Describing a delicate, loosely woven cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax is the plant fibre spun into linen, a raw textile.

clue.text: Leave one in mail shot, to be fair

indicators.note: in places the two pieces inside the rearranged letters of mail
shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters of mail are scrambled

parts.note: to part is to leave or depart
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Taking a break from a mass mailing so things stay even-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' scrambles the letters of 'mail' and 'in' places the other two pieces within; 'Leave' looks like a noun for time off but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Impartial means unbiased, treating all sides equally.

clue.text: Requirements, if born on the outskirts of Dallas

parts.note: née, born, introduces a woman's maiden name

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Things someone needs if they were born at the edge of a Texas city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the outskirts of' takes D and S, the first and last letters of 'Dallas'.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs are things required, necessities.

clue.text: The French bloke looking after the horses wants some space

parts.note: le is the French word for the
a groom is a stable hand who tends horses

explanation.surface: A French stable lad asks for a bit of room to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Legroom is the room for one's legs, as on a plane: a kind of space.

clue.text: Would they load a crude shelter on board ship?

indicators.note: on board means inside the vessel, so the shelter goes between its letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the abbreviation for a ship
a hovel is a crude, wretched dwelling

explanation.surface: Asking whether a makeshift hut might be loaded onto a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a question: shovels are what load things, and 'on board' is the usual ship signal for putting something between S and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Shovels are tools for scooping and loading coal, earth and similar material.

clue.text: Backing favourites with pace

indicators.note: backing here means moving backwards, so the word for favourites is read in reverse

parts.note: favourites, as a teacher's favoured pupils, are pets

explanation.surface: A punter puts money on the favourites because of their speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing favourites' looks like betting language; 'Backing' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pace is a single stride, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Pole wearing Roman clothing in the islands kingdom

indicators.note: wearing means being dressed in, so the pole is wrapped in the garment

parts.note: a toga was the robe worn by Roman citizens
N, north, is one of the two magnetic poles

explanation.surface: A Polish visitor in a toga touring a Pacific monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a person from Poland; it is the North pole, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Polynesian monarchy made up of many islands.

clue.text: Report bats resettling in a place just outside London

indicators.note: resettling means moving to a new position, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bats are reported moving to new homes in a commuter town.
explanation.walkthrough: Potters Bar is a town in Hertfordshire just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Potters Bar is a Hertfordshire town on the northern edge of Greater London.

clue.text: Fruit porter keeping very quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the beer wraps round the musical sign

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: A railway porter tiptoes silently while carrying some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' reads as a luggage carrier but is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple is a common orchard fruit, an example of the class.

clue.text: Establish teachers' source of nourishment

parts.note: to ground an argument is to establish it on a firm base
the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union

explanation.surface: Setting up a school canteen to feed the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT, the National Union of Teachers, was a UK teaching union.
explanation.definitionFit: A groundnut, the peanut, is an edible seed that supplies food.

clue.text: Obtains return in negotiable savings

indicators.note: in puts the turned-round word inside the abbreviation

parts.note: neg. is a short form of negotiable, as in classified price ads

indicators.note: return means coming back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: gets means obtains

explanation.surface: Getting a better rate on flexible savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiable' gives its classified-ad abbreviation; 'return' turns the verb round and 'in' sets it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is money put aside for the future, a reserve.

clue.text: Knight came back only for this dish

indicators.note: came back means the title is turned to face the other way, read backwards

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: A knight returned home just to eat this particular meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came back' reverses SIR to RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rissole is a fried cake of minced meat, a type of savoury plate of food.

clue.text: Avoid excess

definitions.meaning: to ... someone a chore is to let them avoid it
something extra or surplus, more than needed

explanation.definitionFit: To spare is to let off or avoid; as a noun or adjective it means surplus, left over.

clue.text: Delays caused by office workers accepting zero increase

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the workers surround the other pieces

parts.note: temps are temporary office workers
O looks like zero
a rise is an increase

explanation.surface: Agency staff hold things up by refusing a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' signals the workers taking in the other pieces; 'Delays' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To temporise is to stall or play for time.

clue.text: Witty saying in English "one who gorges on sheep"

parts.note: a greedy eater who gorges is called a pig
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: An English insult calling someone a glutton who wolfs down lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short clever remark, a pithy quip.

clue.text: Rose to talk at length on the origin of Richmond

parts.note: to ramble is to talk on and on

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, its first letter

explanation.surface: A gardener holds forth about roses on a visit to Richmond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a verb or a name; it is the climbing flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is a vigorous climbing variety of the garden flower.

clue.text: Safety first — shelves these vehicles

indicators.note: first tells us to take only the opening letter of the word Safety

parts.note: ledges are narrow shelves

explanation.surface: Health and safety comes before shelving, says a warehouse notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes S from 'Safety'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sledges are runners-mounted carriers pulled over snow, a kind of transport.

clue.text: Scrambled egg in real spicy drink

indicators.note: scrambled means mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Breakfast eggs end up in a fizzy soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrambled' rearranges the letters of 'egg in real'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger ale is a fizzy soft drink flavoured with ginger root.

clue.text: Distraught compiler's unfinished heated debate

indicators.note: distraught means upset and in disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order
unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the compiler is the setter of the crossword

explanation.surface: A frazzled setter's half-written argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts COMPILER to COMPILE, and 'Distraught' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A polemic is a fierce written or spoken attack, a strong controversial argument.

clue.text: Island thus sheltered by marine growth, for the most part

indicators.note: sheltered by means held inside, so thus goes into the trimmed reef word
for the most part means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: coral is a growth found in the sea
sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: An island so named because it hides behind a reef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops the last letter of the reef word, and 'sheltered by' tucks the Latin word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsica is a French Mediterranean isle.

clue.text: The shade to which a further degree protects a chap

indicators.note: protects means surrounds and shields, so the degree wraps round the man

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a higher degree taken after a first one
a gent is a chap, a gentleman

explanation.surface: Asking which colour goes with a man who holds a master's degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protects' makes the degree wrap the chap; 'a further degree' looks like a step on a colour scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish-red colour, a hue or shade.

clue.text: Wine and cake?

definitions.meaning: a fortified dessert drink from a Portuguese Atlantic isle
a plain sponge traditionally eaten with that wine

explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a fortified Portuguese drink and also a plain British sponge.

clue.text: Whirl round, quietly drive off

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the spinning word goes about the soft sign

parts.note: to reel is to whirl or spin round
P, piano, is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A dancer spins round and then slips silently away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks part of the spin; it puts REEL around P.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel attackers is to force them back, driving them away.

clue.text: A student's visual aid

definitions.meaning: the opening in the eye that lets light in, so an aid to seeing

explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is a learner at school, and also the dark aperture of the eye.

clue.text: What might perhaps predate bureaucracy?

indicators.note: perhaps signals a possible rearrangement of the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Wondering which came first, paperwork or something older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of 'predate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Red tape is excessive official rules and form-filling, an idiom for officialdom.

clue.text: A way of looking at fish

definitions.meaning: a point of view or slant on something
to fish with rod and line

explanation.definitionFit: An angle is a viewpoint, and to angle is to fish with a hook.

clue.text: Duck rising star's responsibility

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading upward, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: the sun is a star

explanation.surface: A cricketing celebrity's score of nothing becomes a burden to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of zero in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Onus means the burden or duty that falls on someone.

clue.text: Marvellous little outfit producing car!

parts.note: super means marvellous or excellent
a mini is a very short skirt or dress, a small garment

explanation.surface: A fabulous tiny dress unexpectedly turns into a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A supermini is a small hatchback class of motor vehicle.

clue.text: Smile over a bit of corn

indicators.note: over is used here as covering, the broad smile placed over and around the letter

parts.note: a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: Grinning down at a single kernel of maize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts GRIN around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A grain is a single seed or kernel of a cereal crop.

clue.text: An old sea-dog's wit

definitions.meaning: an experienced old sailor is called an old ...
... can mean sharp humour, as in Attic ...

explanation.definitionFit: Salt is slang for a veteran sailor, and also means pungent, clever humour.

clue.text: A charge concealed by fiddling preset boundaries

indicators.note: concealed by means hidden inside, so the first pieces go into the rearranged word
fiddling means tampering, so the letters of preset are rearranged

parts.note: to ram is to charge at something

explanation.surface: A hidden fee buried by tampering with the default limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddling' rearranges PRESET into PETERS, and 'concealed by' places the charge pieces after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Parameters are limits or set bounds within which something operates.
